records.title: 30005461: Motzkin threshold limit 3 and credited mixed odd SOS powers

outcome_quotes.quote: ## Full two-clause mathematical resolution

For arbitrary real polynomials p,q, if p^(2i+1) and q^(2j+1) are sums
of squares, then (p+q)^(2i+2j+1) is a sum of squares. This is the
published Blekherman–Kozhasov–Reznick theorem, with the truncated-binomial
ingredient credited to Iosif Pinelis. The full credited proof, both source
index/display corrections, arbitrary-degree reduction and edge cases are
included.

For f_c=x^4*y^2+x^2*y^4+1-c*x^2*y^2, every fixed real c<3 has all
sufficiently large odd powers SOS, and the thresholds satisfy lim c_k=3.
The complete argument applies Scheiderer's published Corollary 4.2 to a
strictly positive quadratic section on the integral singular cubic ABC=D^3,
lifts all square-root sections with the cubic hypersurface exact sequence,
and substitutes (A,B,C,D)=(x^2*y,x*y^2,z^3,x*y*z). It gives the exact
Motzkin power without a multiplier or denominator. All sign patterns,
singular boundary points, exponent parity, base points and the limit are
checked explicitly in the proof and substantive independent audit.
